+# Coding Standards
+
+## Overview
+
+Standards for the `wandelbots-nova` Python SDK, enforced via `ruff` (lint + format) and `ty` (type checking). Git hooks (husky + lint-staged) auto-run these on staged files at commit time.
+
+## Code Formatting
+
+**Tool**: `ruff format`
+**Config**: `ruff.toml`
+**Enforcement**: Pre-commit hook (husky + lint-staged) and CI
+
+### Key Settings
+
+- **Quote style**: double quotes
+- **Indent style**: spaces (4-width)
+- **Magic trailing comma**: respected (not skipped)
+- **Line ending**: auto-detected
+
+## Linting
+
+**Tool**: `ruff check`
+**Base Config**: `ruff.toml` (root); `novapolicy/pyproject.toml` overrides with max strictness for that module
+**Strictness**: Root — `E4`, `E7`, `E9`, `F`, `UP006`, `TID251` selected
+
+### Key Rules
+
+- `TID251` (banned imports): `icecream` banned in production code — dev dependency only, use proper logging instead
+- `TID251` per-file-ignore: allowed in `**/tests/**`, `test_*.py`, `examples/**`
+- Import sorting (`I`) run separately: `ruff check --select I --fix`
+
+## Naming Conventions
+
+### Files and Folders
+
+- Test files: `test_*.py`, colocated with source or under `tests/`
+- Modules: lowercase, underscore-separated (e.g., `command_routines`, `helper_scripts`)
+
+## File Organization
+
+### Project Structure
+
+```
+nova/                  # Main SDK package
+├── actions/           # Motion primitives (ptp, lin, jnt, cir, collision_free, io_write, wait)
+├── cell/              # Cell/Controller/MotionGroup abstractions
+├── core/              # Core client entry point (Nova)
+├── types/             # Pose, RobotState, MotionSettings, CollisionScene
+├── program/           # @program decorator
+├── events/            # Event/signal handling (blinker)
+├── datasets/          # Dataset utilities
+├── command_routines/  # Command routine helpers
+├── extensions/        # Extension points
+├── viewers/           # Visualization support
+├── utils/             # Shared utilities
+├── logging/           # Loguru-based logging setup
+└── api.py             # Auto-generated API client (wandelbots_api_client re-export)
+
+novax/                 # FastAPI app framework for NOVA apps
+novapolicy/             # Experimental policy execution package
+wandelscript/          # DSL for robot programs
+nova_rerun_bridge/     # 3D visualization bridge
+examples/              # Example NOVA apps and scripts
+tests/                 # Top-level test suite
+docs/                  # Documentation (incl. programs.md quickstart)
+```
+
+### Conventions
+
+- Tests colocated near source (`nova/`, `wandelscript/`) as well as a top-level `tests/` directory
+- `--doctest-modules` enabled in pytest — module docstrings with examples are tested
+
+## Import Order
+
+```python
+# 1. Standard library
+import asyncio
+
+# 2. Third-party
+import httpx
+from pydantic import BaseModel
+
+# 3. Local (nova.*)
+from nova import Nova
+from nova.actions import ptp
+```
+
+**Rules**:
+- Enforced via `ruff check --select I --fix`
+- No manual reordering needed — run the fixer
+
+## Error Handling
+
+### Pattern
+
+**Approach**: Standard Python exceptions; async context managers (`async with Nova() as nova`) for resource cleanup
+
+### Guidelines
+
+- Prefer explicit exception types over bare `except`
+- Use `exceptiongroup` for aggregating multiple async task failures where applicable
+- Resource lifecycle (connections, controllers) managed via async context managers
+
+## Logging
+
+**Tool**: `loguru` (wrapped via `nova.logging.logger`)
+**Format**: Structured, loguru default format
+
+### Guidelines
+
+**Always log**:
+- Connection/controller lifecycle events
+- Motion planning and execution errors
+
+**Never log**:
+- Credentials, tokens, API keys
+- Full robot pose/trajectory data at INFO level (use DEBUG if needed)
+
+## Comments and Documentation
+
+### When to Comment
+
+- Document non-obvious motion planning / limits logic (see `nova-api-v2` skill for planning data-flow specifics)
+- Explain deviations from the released NOVA API v2 spec (e.g., nightly-only fields)
+
+### Documentation Format
+
+**Functions**: Google/NumPy-style docstrings; doctest examples where practical (module docstrings are tested via `--doctest-modules`)
+**Classes**: Docstring summarizing purpose and key public methods
+

+# Project Constitution
+
+> Universal policies that apply to ALL code in this project.
+> This file is always inherited from root — modules cannot override it.
+
+## Git Workflow
+
+- **Commit Style**: Conventional commits (feat:, fix:, chore:, docs:, refactor:, test:) — enforced via `release-please` and PR title check CI
+- **Branch Strategy**: Feature branches merged via pull request
+- **Main Branch**: `main` is always deployable
+
+## Code Review
+
+- All changes require pull request review
+- At least one approval required before merge
+- No self-merging to main
+- Security-sensitive changes require additional review
+
+## CI/CD
+
+- **Platform**: GitHub Actions (`.github/workflows/`)
+- All PRs must pass CI checks before merge (lint, typecheck, tests, CodeQL, dependency review)
+- Automated tests run on every push (`nova-dev.yaml`, `nova-nightly.yaml`)
+- Releases automated via `release-please`
+
+## Security Policies
+
+- **No secrets in code** — use environment variables (`.env`, `python-decouple`) or secret management
+- Dependencies must be from trusted sources; audited via `uv-audit.yaml` CI workflow
+- Security vulnerabilities addressed within SLA
+- No credentials, API keys, or tokens in source control
+
+## Documentation
+
+- Public APIs must be documented (auto-generated docs via `autodocs.yaml`)
+- Breaking changes require migration notes in `CHANGELOG.md`
+- README kept up to date with setup instructions
+- `docs/programs.md` must be kept up to date whenever `@nova.program` or NOVAx behavior changes

+# System Architecture
+
+## Overview
+
+`wandelbots-nova` is the official Python SDK for the Wandelbots NOVA API. NOVA is a robot-agnostic operating system that enables developers to plan, program, control, and operate fleets of six-axis industrial robots through a unified API, across all major robot brands.
+
+## System Context
+
+The SDK is a client library: it connects to a running NOVA instance (API server) over HTTP/WebSocket and exposes a high-level async Python API for controlling robot cells, controllers, and motion groups.
+
+### Context Diagram
+
+```
+ Developer code (@nova.program)
+          │
+          ▼
+   wandelbots-nova SDK (this repo)
+          │  httpx / websockets
+          ▼
+     NOVA API v2 (server)
+          │
+          ▼
+  Robot Controllers (multi-vendor: 6-axis industrial robots)
+```
+
+### Users
+
+- **SDK developers**: Python developers writing programs to control robot cells via `Nova`, `Cell`, `Controller`, `MotionGroup`
+- **NOVAx app developers**: Build and deploy FastAPI-based NOVA apps that host `@nova.program` functions
+
+### External Systems
+
+- **NOVA API v2**: The released robot-agnostic control API this SDK targets (source of truth via `wandelbots_api_client`)
+- **Robot controllers**: Multi-vendor six-axis industrial robot hardware, accessed indirectly through NOVA
+
+## Architecture Pattern
+
+**Pattern**: Layered SDK — generated API client at the base, high-level async abstractions (`Nova`, `Cell`, `Controller`, `MotionGroup`) on top, optional extras (NOVAx, wandelscript, nova_rerun_bridge, novapolicy) built on the core SDK
+**Rationale**: Keeps the core small and API-spec-aligned while allowing optional feature packages to be installed only when needed
+
+## Component Architecture
+
+### Components
+
+#### nova (core SDK)
+
+- **Purpose**: High-level async client for the NOVA API
+- **Responsibilities**: Cell/controller/motion-group management, motion planning (`plan_trajectory`), execution, program decorator, types (Pose, RobotState, MotionSettings, CollisionScene)
+- **Dependencies**: `wandelbots_api_client` (as `nova.api`), httpx, websockets, pydantic
+
+#### novax
+
+- **Purpose**: App framework for building FastAPI server applications
+- **Responsibilities**: Program registration/scanning, lifecycle management, `nova app create`/`nova app install` CLI scaffolding, Skaffold-based hot reload for deployment
+- **Dependencies**: nova, fastapi, uvicorn
+
+#### wandelscript
+
+- **Purpose**: DSL for writing robot programs
+- **Responsibilities**: Parsing (antlr4-generated), execution of wandelscript programs against the SDK
+- **Dependencies**: nova, antlr4-python3-runtime, geometricalgebra
+
+#### nova_rerun_bridge
+
+- **Purpose**: 3D visualization of robot trajectories
+- **Responsibilities**: Bridges SDK trajectory/pose data to rerun-sdk for visualization
+- **Dependencies**: nova, rerun-sdk, trimesh
+
+#### novapolicy (experimental)
+
+- **Purpose**: Waypoint-jogging-based policy execution for NOVA robots
+- **Responsibilities**: Experimental policy-driven robot control
+- **Dependencies**: nova, aiortc, pyzmq
+
+### Component Diagram
+
+```
+             ┌────────────┐
+             │   nova     │  (core)
+             └─────┬──────┘
+     ┌──────┬──────┼───────┬────────────┐
+     ▼      ▼      ▼       ▼            ▼
+  novax  wandelscript  nova_rerun_bridge  novapolicy
+```
+
+## Data Flow
+
+Programs written against the SDK call into `Nova`/`Cell`/`Controller`/`MotionGroup`, which translate high-level motion actions (ptp, lin, jnt, cir, etc.) into `plan_trajectory` requests sent to the NOVA API v2 server; the resulting trajectory is then executed against the target motion group.
+
+```
+Actions (ptp, lin, jnt, cir, ...)
+        │
+        ▼
+MotionGroup.plan(actions, tcp)  ──►  NOVA API v2 (plan_trajectory)
+        │
+        ▼
+Trajectory
+        │
+        ▼
+MotionGroup.execute(trajectory, tcp, actions)  ──►  NOVA API v2  ──►  Robot Controller
+```
+
+## Technology Stack
+
+| Layer | Technology | Purpose |
+|-------|------------|---------|
+| SDK core | Python 3.12+, pydantic, httpx, websockets | Async client for NOVA API v2 |
+| App framework | FastAPI, uvicorn (novax) | Serve `@nova.program` functions as apps |
+| DSL | wandelscript, antlr4 | Scripted robot programs |
+| Visualization | rerun-sdk, trimesh | 3D trajectory visualization |
+| Messaging | nats-py, asyncua | Messaging/OPC UA integration |
+| Tooling | uv, ruff, ty, pytest | Package management, lint/format, type check, tests |
+| CI/CD | GitHub Actions | Build, test, release automation |
+
+## Non-Functional Requirements
+
+### Security
+
+- No secrets committed to source control; use environment variables (`python-decouple`)
+- Dependency vulnerability auditing via `uv-audit.yaml`
+
+### Scalability
+
+Robot cell/controller/motion-group abstractions are designed to manage fleets of robots concurrently via async I/O (asyncio, anyio, aiostream).
+
+## Constraints
+
+- Must track the **released** NOVA API v2 (`wandelbots_api_client`), not unreleased/nightly spec fields — see `nova-api-v2` skill for verification workflow
+- `docs/programs.md` must stay in sync with `@nova.program` / NOVAx behavior changes
+
+---

+# Testing Standards
+
+## Overview
+
+Test suite for `wandelbots-nova`, using `pytest` with async support and doctest integration.
+
+## Testing Framework
+
+**Framework**: pytest
+**Runner**: `uv run pytest`
+
+## Test Types
+
+| Type | Tool | Location | When to Use |
+|------|------|----------|-------------|
+| Unit | pytest | `tests/`, `nova/**/test_*.py`, `wandelscript/tests/` | Default for all new logic |
+| Doctest | pytest (`--doctest-modules`) | Module docstrings | Public API usage examples |
+| Integration | pytest (marker: `integration`) | `tests/`, module test dirs | Requires a running NOVA instance |
+| Policy tests | pytest | `novapolicy/tests/` | novapolicy-specific behavior |
+
+## Coverage Requirements
+
+**Target**: Not enforced via a numeric gate in CI; contributions expected to include tests for new/changed behavior
+**Enforcement**: CI runs full unit test suite (excluding `integration`) on every push/PR
+
+**Critical paths that MUST have coverage:**
+- Motion planning (`plan_trajectory`, `MotionGroupSetup`, `LimitSet`, `LimitsOverride`)
+- `@nova.program` decorator behavior and `ProgramContext`
+- NOVAx registration/serving behavior
+
+## Test Naming
+
+**Pattern**: `test_<behavior>`
+
+**Examples**:
+- `test_plan_trajectory_respects_limits` — verifies planning honors limit overrides
+- `test_program_context_input_schema` — verifies program input-schema derivation
+
+## Running Tests
+
+```bash
+# Run all unit tests (excluding integration tests)
+PYTHONPATH=. uv run pytest -rs -v -m "not integration"
+
+# Run a single test file
+PYTHONPATH=. uv run pytest -rs -v path/to/test_file.py
+
+# Run a specific test
+PYTHONPATH=. uv run pytest -rs -v path/to/test_file.py::test_function_name
+```
+
+## CI/CD Integration
+
+**Pipeline**: GitHub Actions (`nova-dev.yaml`, `nova-nightly.yaml`)
+**Trigger**: Push and pull request
+
+**Required gates**:
+- `ruff check .` (lint)
+- `uv run ty check` (type checking)
+- `pytest -m "not integration"` (unit tests)
+- CodeQL analysis (`codeql.yaml`)
+- Dependency review (`dependency-review.yaml`)
+- `uv-audit.yaml` (dependency vulnerability audit)
+
+---

# Activate FIRE

**Command**: `/specsmd-fire`

---

## Activation

You are now the **FIRE Orchestrator** for specsmd.

**IMMEDIATELY** read and adopt the persona from:
→ `.specsmd/fire/agents/orchestrator/agent.md`

---

## Critical First Steps

1. **Read Config**: `.specsmd/fire/memory-bank.yaml`
2. **Check Initialization**: Verify `.specs-fire/state.yaml` exists
3. **If NOT initialized** → Execute `project-init` skill
4. **If initialized** → Execute `route` skill to determine next action

---

## Your Skills

- **Project Init**: `.specsmd/fire/agents/orchestrator/skills/project-init/SKILL.md` → Initialize new project
- **Route**: `.specsmd/fire/agents/orchestrator/skills/route/SKILL.md` → Route to appropriate agent
- **Status**: `.specsmd/fire/agents/orchestrator/skills/status/SKILL.md` → Show project status

---

## Routing Targets

- **Planning**: Planner Agent → `/specsmd-fire-planner`
- **Building**: Builder Agent → `/specsmd-fire-builder`

---

## Begin

Activate now. Read your agent definition and start the orchestration process.

Official Python SDK for the Wandelbots NOVA API. NOVA is a robot-agnostic operating system that enables developers to plan, program, control, and operate fleets of six-axis industrial robots through a unified API, across all major robot brands.
## Project Overview


**Requirements**: Python >=3.12

## Build & Development Commands

```bash
# Install dependencies
uv sync --extra "nova-rerun-bridge"
# Format code
uv run ruff format

# Lint and import sorting
uv run ruff check --select I --fix
uv run ruff check .

# Type checking
uv run ty check

PYTHONPATH=. uv run pytest -rs -v -m "not integration"
# Run all unit tests (excluding integration tests)

# Run a single test file
PYTHONPATH=. uv run pytest -rs -v path/to/test_file.py

# Run a specific test
PYTHONPATH=. uv run pytest -rs -v path/to/test_file.py::test_function_name

# Git hooks (husky + lint-staged): auto-format/lint staged files on commit
npm install          # one-time setup: activates the husky pre-commit hook
npx lint-staged      # run the hook manually against staged files

# Build package
uv build

# Download robot models for visualization
uv run download-models

## Architecture Overview


This SDK enables Python developers to control industrial robots through the Wandelbots NOVA API.
### Core Packages
- **nova/**: Main SDK package

  - `Nova` - High-level client entry point (uses async context manager pattern)
  - `Cell` - Represents a robot cell containing controllers
  - `Controller` - Manages robot controller hardware connections
  - `MotionGroup` - Handles motion planning and execution for a robot arm
  - `actions/` - Motion primitives: `ptp`, `lin`, `jnt`, `cir`, `collision_free`, `io_write`, `wait`
  - `types/` - Data types: `Pose`, `RobotState`, `MotionSettings`, `CollisionScene`
  - `program/` - `@program` decorator for defining executable robot programs
  - `api.py` - Auto-generated API client (via `wandelbots_api_client`)

- **novax/**: App framework for building FastAPI server applications
  - `Novax` - FastAPI integration with program registration and lifecycle management
  - Used with `nova app create` CLI to scaffold new apps
```

### Core Usage Pattern
```python
from nova import Nova

async with Nova() as nova:
    cell = nova.cell()
    controller = await cell.controller("robot-name")
    motion_group = controller[0]

    actions = [joint_ptp(joints), linear(pose)]
    trajectory = await motion_group.plan(actions, tcp)
    await motion_group.execute(trajectory, tcp, actions=actions)
```

# Coding Standards

## Overview

Standards for the `wandelbots-nova` Python SDK, enforced via `ruff` (lint + format) and `ty` (type checking). Git hooks (husky + lint-staged) auto-run these on staged files at commit time.

## Code Formatting

**Tool**: `ruff format`
**Config**: `ruff.toml`
**Enforcement**: Pre-commit hook (husky + lint-staged) and CI

### Key Settings

- **Quote style**: double quotes
- **Indent style**: spaces (4-width)
- **Magic trailing comma**: respected (not skipped)
- **Line ending**: auto-detected

## Linting

**Tool**: `ruff check`
**Base Config**: `ruff.toml` (root); `novapolicy/pyproject.toml` overrides with max strictness for that module
**Strictness**: Root — `E4`, `E7`, `E9`, `F`, `UP006`, `TID251` selected

### Key Rules

- `TID251` (banned imports): `icecream` banned in production code — dev dependency only, use proper logging instead
- `TID251` per-file-ignore: allowed in `**/tests/**`, `test_*.py`, `examples/**`
- Import sorting (`I`) run separately: `ruff check --select I --fix`

## Naming Conventions

### Files and Folders

- Test files: `test_*.py`, colocated with source or under `tests/`
- Modules: lowercase, underscore-separated (e.g., `command_routines`, `helper_scripts`)

## File Organization

### Project Structure

```
nova/                  # Main SDK package
├── actions/           # Motion primitives (ptp, lin, jnt, cir, collision_free, io_write, wait)
├── cell/              # Cell/Controller/MotionGroup abstractions
├── core/              # Core client entry point (Nova)
├── types/             # Pose, RobotState, MotionSettings, CollisionScene
├── program/           # @program decorator
├── events/            # Event/signal handling (blinker)
├── datasets/          # Dataset utilities
├── command_routines/  # Command routine helpers
├── extensions/        # Extension points
├── viewers/           # Visualization support
├── utils/             # Shared utilities
├── logging/           # Loguru-based logging setup
└── api.py             # Auto-generated API client (wandelbots_api_client re-export)

novax/                 # FastAPI app framework for NOVA apps
novapolicy/             # Experimental policy execution package
wandelscript/          # DSL for robot programs
nova_rerun_bridge/     # 3D visualization bridge
examples/              # Example NOVA apps and scripts
tests/                 # Top-level test suite
docs/                  # Documentation (incl. programs.md quickstart)
```

### Conventions

- Tests colocated near source (`nova/`, `wandelscript/`) as well as a top-level `tests/` directory
- `--doctest-modules` enabled in pytest — module docstrings with examples are tested

## Import Order

```python
# 1. Standard library
import asyncio

# 2. Third-party
import httpx
from pydantic import BaseModel

# 3. Local (nova.*)
from nova import Nova
from nova.actions import ptp
```

**Rules**:
- Enforced via `ruff check --select I --fix`
- No manual reordering needed — run the fixer

## Error Handling

### Pattern

**Approach**: Standard Python exceptions; async context managers (`async with Nova() as nova`) for resource cleanup

### Guidelines

- Prefer explicit exception types over bare `except`
- Use `exceptiongroup` for aggregating multiple async task failures where applicable
- Resource lifecycle (connections, controllers) managed via async context managers

## Logging

**Tool**: `loguru` (wrapped via `nova.logging.logger`)
**Format**: Structured, loguru default format

### Guidelines

**Always log**:
- Connection/controller lifecycle events
- Motion planning and execution errors

**Never log**:
- Credentials, tokens, API keys
- Full robot pose/trajectory data at INFO level (use DEBUG if needed)

## Comments and Documentation

### When to Comment

- Document non-obvious motion planning / limits logic (see `nova-api-v2` skill for planning data-flow specifics)
- Explain deviations from the released NOVA API v2 spec (e.g., nightly-only fields)

### Documentation Format

**Functions**: Google/NumPy-style docstrings; doctest examples where practical (module docstrings are tested via `--doctest-modules`)
**Classes**: Docstring summarizing purpose and key public methods

# System Architecture

## Overview

`wandelbots-nova` is the official Python SDK for the Wandelbots NOVA API. NOVA is a robot-agnostic operating system that enables developers to plan, program, control, and operate fleets of six-axis industrial robots through a unified API, across all major robot brands.

## System Context

The SDK is a client library: it connects to a running NOVA instance (API server) over HTTP/WebSocket and exposes a high-level async Python API for controlling robot cells, controllers, and motion groups.

### Context Diagram

```
 Developer code (@nova.program)
          │
          ▼
   wandelbots-nova SDK (this repo)
          │  httpx / websockets
          ▼
     NOVA API v2 (server)
          │
          ▼
  Robot Controllers (multi-vendor: 6-axis industrial robots)
```

### Users

- **SDK developers**: Python developers writing programs to control robot cells via `Nova`, `Cell`, `Controller`, `MotionGroup`
- **NOVAx app developers**: Build and deploy FastAPI-based NOVA apps that host `@nova.program` functions

### External Systems

- **NOVA API v2**: The released robot-agnostic control API this SDK targets (source of truth via `wandelbots_api_client`)
- **Robot controllers**: Multi-vendor six-axis industrial robot hardware, accessed indirectly through NOVA

## Architecture Pattern

**Pattern**: Layered SDK — generated API client at the base, high-level async abstractions (`Nova`, `Cell`, `Controller`, `MotionGroup`) on top, optional extras (NOVAx, wandelscript, nova_rerun_bridge, novapolicy) built on the core SDK
**Rationale**: Keeps the core small and API-spec-aligned while allowing optional feature packages to be installed only when needed

## Component Architecture

### Components

#### nova (core SDK)

- **Purpose**: High-level async client for the NOVA API
- **Responsibilities**: Cell/controller/motion-group management, motion planning (`plan_trajectory`), execution, program decorator, types (Pose, RobotState, MotionSettings, CollisionScene)
- **Dependencies**: `wandelbots_api_client` (as `nova.api`), httpx, websockets, pydantic

#### novax

- **Purpose**: App framework for building FastAPI server applications
- **Responsibilities**: Program registration/scanning, lifecycle management, `nova app create`/`nova app install` CLI scaffolding, Skaffold-based hot reload for deployment
- **Dependencies**: nova, fastapi, uvicorn

#### wandelscript

- **Purpose**: DSL for writing robot programs
- **Responsibilities**: Parsing (antlr4-generated), execution of wandelscript programs against the SDK
- **Dependencies**: nova, antlr4-python3-runtime, geometricalgebra

#### nova_rerun_bridge

- **Purpose**: 3D visualization of robot trajectories
- **Responsibilities**: Bridges SDK trajectory/pose data to rerun-sdk for visualization
- **Dependencies**: nova, rerun-sdk, trimesh

#### novapolicy (experimental)

- **Purpose**: Waypoint-jogging-based policy execution for NOVA robots
- **Responsibilities**: Experimental policy-driven robot control
- **Dependencies**: nova, aiortc, pyzmq

### Component Diagram

```
             ┌────────────┐
             │   nova     │  (core)
             └─────┬──────┘
     ┌──────┬──────┼───────┬────────────┐
     ▼      ▼      ▼       ▼            ▼
  novax  wandelscript  nova_rerun_bridge  novapolicy
```

## Data Flow

Programs written against the SDK call into `Nova`/`Cell`/`Controller`/`MotionGroup`, which translate high-level motion actions (ptp, lin, jnt, cir, etc.) into `plan_trajectory` requests sent to the NOVA API v2 server; the resulting trajectory is then executed against the target motion group.

```
Actions (ptp, lin, jnt, cir, ...)
        │
        ▼
MotionGroup.plan(actions, tcp)  ──►  NOVA API v2 (plan_trajectory)
        │
        ▼
Trajectory
        │
        ▼
MotionGroup.execute(trajectory, tcp, actions)  ──►  NOVA API v2  ──►  Robot Controller
```

## Technology Stack

| Layer | Technology | Purpose |
|-------|------------|---------|
| SDK core | Python 3.12+, pydantic, httpx, websockets | Async client for NOVA API v2 |
| App framework | FastAPI, uvicorn (novax) | Serve `@nova.program` functions as apps |
| DSL | wandelscript, antlr4 | Scripted robot programs |
| Visualization | rerun-sdk, trimesh | 3D trajectory visualization |
| Messaging | nats-py, asyncua | Messaging/OPC UA integration |
| Tooling | uv, ruff, ty, pytest | Package management, lint/format, type check, tests |
| CI/CD | GitHub Actions | Build, test, release automation |

## Non-Functional Requirements

### Security

- No secrets committed to source control; use environment variables (`python-decouple`)
- Dependency vulnerability auditing via `uv-audit.yaml`

### Scalability

Robot cell/controller/motion-group abstractions are designed to manage fleets of robots concurrently via async I/O (asyncio, anyio, aiostream).

## Constraints

- Must track the **released** NOVA API v2 (`wandelbots_api_client`), not unreleased/nightly spec fields — see `nova-api-v2` skill for verification workflow
- `docs/programs.md` must stay in sync with `@nova.program` / NOVAx behavior changes
